source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 9. Exercises reused from the lesson; du'aas flagged for review.
topic: A building with five pillars stands firm

learn.en: Islam is built on five pillars: five duties every Muslim must do.
learn.title: Five pillars

learn.en: 1. Ash-Shahadah: there is no god worthy of worship but Allah, and Muhammad is His Messenger.
learn.title: The Shahadah
learn.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللهِ

learn.en: 2. Salah: praying five times every day. 3. Zakah: rich Muslims give to the poor and needy.
learn.title: Salah and Zakah

learn.en: 4. Sawm: fasting in Ramadan. 5. Hajj: visiting the Ka'bah once in a lifetime, for those who are able.
learn.title: Sawm and Hajj

learn.en: A building with five strong pillars stands firm. If Muslims do these five things well, Islam stays firm.
learn.title: Standing firm

learn.en: “And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow.” (Qur'an 2:43)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

words.ar: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللهِ
words.en: The Shahadah: no god but Allah, Muhammad is His Messenger

order.en: Put the five pillars in order

quiz.en: Praying five times a day is…
Giving money to those who need it is…
Fasting in the month of Ramadan is…
Saying lā ilāha illa-llāh, Muḥammadun rasūlu-llāh is…

think.q: Which of the five pillars can you do already, and which will you do when you are older?
think.a: The Shahadah and salah now; fasting a little; zakah and Hajj when you are able.

parents.summary: The five pillars: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm (Ramadan), Hajj — like five pillars holding up a building.
parents.tip: Build a little house with 5 pillars from blocks and label them.
